svg.title: Getting Booked by Insurance Relocation Companies
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-insurance-relocation-booking-flow; chapter number: 1; chart type: process_flow; title: Getting Booked by Insurance Relocation Companies; subtitle: From portal listing to a signed, utility-capped agreement; caption: Five practitioner-tested moves for landing displaced families: list in agency portals, confirm by phone, run specialist email blasts, let the agency name the number, and cap utilities before signing.; assumptions note: Figures are attributed practitioner claims. The $8,100 house versus about $15,000 a month in hotel rooms is one family-of-seven case reported by Jesse Vasquez, not a market average.; note: Sources include Bailey Kramer (DFn2vbuykUY, J-7ks576i8Q), The Bougie Baldie (PaAH8z8rPe8), Dr Chau Ong (Bbit4NDO_Hc), and Jesse Vasquez (Ncr7TdF1G34, O1Wmu9p-zdc).; stages: step: 01; label: List on ALE Solutions and THD; value: Step 1; detail: Put a realistic number on the ALE Solutions form; the listed price is not the price you charge and gets renegotiated after the match (Bailey Kramer).; step: 02; label: Confirm every submission by phone; value: Step 2; detail: Call within a week, because the form gives no confirmation and can create duplicate entries (The Bougie Baldie).; step: 03; label: Email specialists on a cadence; value: Step 3; detail: Weekly or biweekly blasts with a PS asking specialists to forward and a PPS offering referrals in other cities, so ten contacts become twenty (Bailey Kramer).; step: 04; label: Let the agency name the number; value: Step 4; detail: Ask for the price range per night, never the budget (Dr Chau Ong). Anchor against the hotel bill, such as $8,100 a month versus about $15,000 in two rooms (Jesse Vasquez).; step: 05; label: Cap utilities before signing; value: Step 5; detail: Write electric and water caps into the agreement and notes, such as the guest paying electric above $500; uncapped electric ran about $1,000 a month on the $8,100 house (Jesse Vasquez).
